findings.issue: Task 13 declares wave: 5 and depends_on: [6, 12], but Task 12 is also wave: 5. Validator rule: dependent task's wave MUST be strictly greater than dependency's wave. Task 13 in wave 5 cannot depend on Task 12 in wave 5 — same-wave tasks execute in parallel, but Task 13 needs Task 12 done first.
findings.fix: Either bump Task 13 to wave 6 (and Task 14 to wave 7) to express strict sequential ordering, OR document and accept the convention that the Final Wave executes sequentially per teammate_name (qa-runner → deployer → post-deploy-qa). If the orchestrator (feature-execution skill) treats Final Wave as a sequential chain when depends_on links exist within the wave, document this exception in tech-spec §Implementation Tasks header. As written, the wave numbers do not encode the actual execution ordering.

findings.issue: Task 14 declares wave: 5 and depends_on: [13], but Task 13 is also wave: 5. Same-wave-with-internal-dependency anti-pattern as Task 13 → 12. Per validator rule, dependent task's wave must be strictly greater.
findings.fix: Bump Task 14 wave to 7 (or 6 if Task 13 stays at 5) so the wave field encodes actual execution ordering. Alternatively, formally document Final Wave sequential-by-depends_on convention in tech-spec.

findings.issue: Task 12 wave 5 with deps [9, 10, 11] is valid (audit waves at 4). However, the cluster of tasks 12, 13, 14 all in wave 5 with internal sequential dependencies is structurally inconsistent with the wave-as-parallel-unit semantics applied to earlier waves (1-4). This is a top-level structural smell, not a bug in Task 12 itself.
findings.fix: If feature-execution skill treats the Final Wave as sequential when depends_on links exist within it, accept and document. Otherwise re-number to waves 5/6/7 to make the ordering explicit and parser-clear. Recommend bumping 13→6 and 14→7 to align with the rest of the decomposition's convention (wave is a parallelism unit).

findings.issue: Task 3 title says 'news_bot.py wiring (import + dispatcher + NETLOC_TO_SOURCE + SOURCE_HASHTAG_OVERRIDE + archived consumer dicts) + sources_registry test extension'. The title is long but accurately reflects the merged scope after round-1 fix (sources_registry test extension was moved in from Task 5). This is acceptable; the long title makes scope unambiguous. No fix needed but flag for awareness.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is. Optional: shorten title to 'news_bot.py wiring + sources_registry test extension'; full scope already enumerated in body.

findings.issue: Task 4 declares depends_on: []. Task 4 says 'парсер `t_hunted_source.py` (Task 1) вызовет `filter_boilerplate` уже с готовыми PT-паттернами после merge waves' — i.e. Task 1's parser will use the PT patterns added by Task 4. There is no hard runtime dependency (filter_boilerplate accepts any pattern list), and Task 4 unit tests don't import t_hunted_source. So depends_on: [] is technically correct. However, semantically Task 4 and Task 1 must both be done before the integration smoke test (Task 8) can verify cross-language behaviour. The current decomposition handles this via Task 8 depends_on: [1, 3] — but Task 4 isn't in Task 8's depends_on either, even though the integration test scenario uses PT content that conceptually relies on Task 4's PT patterns landing. In practice, Task 8 mocks fetch_full_article so the parser+filter path isn't exercised, so it's still acceptable.
findings.fix: No fix required. Optional: add a 'Cross-task notes' line in Task 4 explicitly noting that Task 4 lands in parallel with Task 1 and is not a runtime dependency for Task 1 (PT patterns appended to flat list, no new API).

findings.section: What to do (Out of scope clause)
findings.issue: Task 5 contains a clear 'Out of scope (moved to Task 3)' clause for sources_registry test edits — exactly as instructed by round-1 fix. Cross-reference with Task 3 confirms Task 3 picked up the work. This is clean and consistent. Flagging for completeness, not as a defect.
findings.fix: No fix required — round-1 fix correctly applied.

findings.issue: Tech-spec §Shared resources says 'None. No singleton resources are introduced.' Task 3 introduces a new module-level mutable dict `SOURCE_HASHTAG_OVERRIDE` in news_bot.py. While this isn't a singleton in the traditional sense (no instance, no shared state across processes), it IS a new module-level data structure read by other code paths (`_source_hashtag`). Task 3 correctly notes 'dict is used read-only' but tech-spec wording could be tightened to acknowledge this addition.
findings.fix: Optional: update tech-spec §Shared resources to explicitly note `SOURCE_HASHTAG_OVERRIDE` as a new module-level constant (Decision 2), parallel to existing `NETLOC_TO_SOURCE` / `SOURCE_EMOJI` / `SOURCE_LABEL`. This is documentation hygiene, not a structural bug. Task 3 itself handles ownership correctly: single creator (Task 3), single reader (`_source_hashtag` via same task), no competing instances.

findings.issue: Task 8 depends_on: [1, 3]. Task 8 mocks fetch_full_article entirely and doesn't dispatch to t_hunted_source — so technically only Task 3 (NETLOC_TO_SOURCE mapping for source_name resolution) is required at runtime. However, Task 8's file scope mentions reading t_hunted_source.py for context; and the import chain `import news_bot` (which imports t_hunted_source after Task 3) requires t_hunted_source.py to exist on disk. So depends_on: [1, 3] is correct.
findings.fix: No fix required — depends_on correctly captures both transitive and contextual dependencies.
